payload.claim: `_read_file` gets file content via `runtime.exec_`, whose `Completed.stdout` is produced by `_decode()` in runtime.py (`data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")`) — any byte in the source file that is not valid UTF-8 is silently replaced with U+FFFD before `source_mutated` ever sees the content. `_write_file` (line 376-378) then re-encodes that already-lossy `str` with `.encode()` and overwrites the whole file, so any file that isn't clean UTF-8 (a Latin-1-declared source file, a stray non-UTF-8 byte in a docstring or fixture) gets silently corrupted outside the intended find/replace span for the whole duration of the mutated block. The sibling host implementation this spec is explicitly modeled on (`saffron/mutation.py`) reads and writes raw bytes for exactly this reason ('byte-identical, including a trailing newline or a CRLF line ending that text mode would otherwise normalize away') but that invariant is dropped here without comment — it happens to hold for this repo's own ASCII/UTF-8 source (where gates and tests pass) but is not guaranteed for an arbitrary target repo in production.
